title: Samkhya (the 24 principles
hook: packing up a kitchen box by box, and Samkhya's inventory of everything

segments.voice: Yesterday in Samkhya: buddhi, which decides, and ahamkara, the I-maker that says mine. Did you catch the tag arriving? Day one thousand one hundred seventy-five.

Moving day. The kitchen has to go into boxes, and the only way through it is a list. Plates. Glasses. The pans, which nest. The drawer of things nobody can name. Halfway through, something happens. Listing it all makes the kitchen strange. You see objects you've walked past for years. A list isn't just a record. It's a way of looking. Samkhya made an inventory too, and a much bigger one: everything that exists, sorted into a short list of principles. A few days ago we saw the outline of that count. Today we open the boxes and name what's inside.
screen: `MOVING DAY.` → `A LIST IS A WAY OF LOOKING.` → `OPENING THE BOXES.`

segments.voice: The Samkhya Karika sorts everything with one question: does it come from something, and does something come from it? The root, prakriti, makes but isn't made. Then the Karika names seven that are both made and making: the great one, buddhi; the I-maker, ahamkara; and five subtle elements, the bare potentials of sound, touch, form, taste and smell. Then it names sixteen that are made and make nothing further. Ten of them are the organs. Five take in the world: ear, skin, eye, tongue, nose. Five act on it: speech, hands, feet, and the organs of release and of birth. One more is manas, the mind, which the Karika says shares in both kinds, turning what comes in into a plan. And the last five are the elements you can stub your toe on: space, air, fire, water, earth. One root, seven, sixteen. Now the twenty-four principles in our title have names. And then the Karika names one more thing, and it's set apart from the whole list: purusha, which is neither made nor making. Look at what the inventory does. Everything on the list but the root comes from something, and all of it changes. Your senses, your mind, your sense of I, the floor under you. Purusha is the one thing that doesn't come out of a box. Some students of Samkhya learn this list by heart, not as trivia, but so that, looking at anything, they can ask where it sits in the count.
screen: `ONE QUESTION: MADE, OR MAKING?` · `THE ROOT, THEN SEVEN, THEN SIXTEEN.` · `SENSES, MIND, ELEMENTS.` · `PURUSHA STANDS OUTSIDE THE COUNT.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: walk the count for two minutes. Sit, and let your breath settle. Then go slowly through the list in your own body. Hearing: what sounds are here? Touch: where does your weight land? Seeing, even with your eyes closed. Tasting, smelling. Then your hands, your feet, your voice at rest. Then the mind, already making plans. Each one is on the list. Then just rest, and let the one who's been noticing all of it stay unnamed. The bell holds the time.
Samkhya. Its inventory: one root, seven made and making, sixteen made only. Twenty-four principles, and purusha, the witness, outside the list.
Your line: Samkhya, the twenty-four principles. Today, pick one ordinary moment and ask where it sits in the count: a sense, the mind, the I, or an element. Day one thousand one hundred seventy-five.

howItsDone: Some students of Samkhya memorize the list of principles, the tattvas, from prakriti down to the elements, and teachers in Samkhya and Yoga lineages use it as a map for contemplation.

original.note: Sanskrit: a principle, one of the items in Samkhya's count of what exists.

trapdoor: what you thought: twenty-four principles sounds like a list of rules.
what it means: an inventory of everything that exists, sorted by whether it is made, makes something, or both.
what a scholar hears: Samkhya Karika 3, which sorts the root, the seven and the sixteen, and sets purusha apart as neither product nor producer.

sources.ref: Samkhya Karika 3 (the root unproduced; the seven productive and produced; the sixteen produced; purusha neither)
Samkhya Karika 26–27 (the five organs of sense, the five of action, and manas, which partakes of both)
Samkhya Karika 22, 38 (the subtle elements and the gross elements from them)

notes: The count 1 + 7 + 16 = 24 is built from Karika 3; the total 'twenty-four' is the outline's own number. Many accounts count purusha as the twenty-fifth tattva; the script says purusha 'stands outside the count' instead. Confirm the framing.

Lists: the seven = mahat/buddhi, ahamkara, five tanmatras (sound, touch, form, taste, smell); the sixteen = five jnanendriyas (ear, skin, eye, tongue, nose), five karmendriyas (speech, hands, feet, organs of excretion and generation), manas, five gross elements (space, air, fire, water, earth). Confirm order and glosses.
Manas 'shares in both kinds' and 'turns what comes in into a plan' paraphrases Karika 27 (manas as deliberative, of the nature of both). Confirm.
'Students of Samkhya learn this list by heart' is general; soften or cut if a Keeper prefers.
